summary: A program read a large part of a workspace, then sent a large amount, or kept retrying, to somewhere that is not a model service it uses.

thresholds_explained.window_ms: How long after the agent finished reading the workspace its traffic is still linked to the read for the burst and total tests (30 minutes). Traffic after this is still counted by the whole-run test below.
thresholds_explained.harvest_files: How many files the agent must read under one folder before that folder counts as a workspace it harvested (500). Below this nothing in this rule fires.
thresholds_explained.harvest_history_files: The same, counting only files from .git history (50). History holds deleted secrets, so a smaller read of it is enough.
thresholds_explained.egress_bytes: Total bytes sent to places that are not the agent's own service, inside the window, that fire on their own whatever the workspace size (10 MB).
thresholds_explained.egress_attempts: Connection attempts to one place that count as retrying (20). Only counts when that place also received 1 MB or more, so a telemetry ping that retries does not fire.
thresholds_explained.burst_percent_other: A burst is the most bytes sent to one owner within 5 minutes. A burst to any owner other than the agent's own service fires when it is at least this percent of the workspace (20%). Kept low because an archive compresses.
thresholds_explained.burst_percent_own: The same percent for the agent's own model service (100%). Prompts carry parts of files, so only about the whole workspace at once counts.
thresholds_explained.burst_floor_bytes: No burst smaller than this fires, however small the workspace (256 KB). Stops a tiny repository making every request look like an upload.
thresholds_explained.own_service_floor_bytes: No burst to the agent's own service smaller than this fires (32 MB). A long normal session keeps re-sending its context to the vendor and would otherwise creep past 100% of a small repository. Cost: a small upload to the agent's own vendor does not fire.
thresholds_explained.run_percent_other: Whole-run test: bytes sent to one owner other than the agent's own service, added up over the run's whole life after the read began, fire at this percent of the workspace (50%). Catches a slow trickle or pieces sent long after the read. Higher than the burst's 20% because a whole run also carries ordinary traffic.
thresholds_explained.run_floor_bytes: No whole-run total smaller than this fires (1 MB), so hours of telemetry to one service stay quiet.
thresholds_explained.secret_egress_window_ms: After a secret file is read, how long an outbound burst is still linked to it (10 minutes). A secret is small and leaves in one request, so this is short.

object_storage_note: A plain entry matches a name equal to it or ending in it. 'prefix*.suffix' matches a name ending in .suffix with a label before it that starts with prefix.
model_services_note: An agent's own services: its model API and the vendor's app backend. Not exempt: held to the burst test, so a whole-workspace upload to the vendor still fires.
burst_note: A burst is the most bytes sent to one owner within 5 minutes, compared with the size of the workspace the agent read. Addresses are grouped by owner first: by the owner of their name when it is known, otherwise by network (/24 for IPv4, /48 for IPv6), and all of the agent's own services form one group. One vendor's many addresses are one place, so an upload split across them is still one burst.
